reason: The cited evidence does not address the specific alloy, its AM microstructure, or the proposed twin-strain mechanism. E2 discusses Al addition effects on oxidation in a different HEA, E3 covers spallation resistance in unrelated alloys, and E1 contradicts the premise of protective Al/Ti-rich scale formation. The key premises thus lack direct, accurately represented support.
premises: Pre-existing deformation twins in the AM HEA cause local elastic undulations at high temperature
These undulations concentrate strain at the oxide/substrate interface
The strain concentration causes cracking and spallation of a Ti- and Al-rich oxide scale
Cyclic oxidation and spallation lead to localized embrittlement and catastrophic failure
Reducing oxygen partial pressure minimizes oxide formation and delays failure
